# Sketchi Playground

The Sketchi Playground turns a plain-language prompt into a clean, editable
diagram. People use it at https://playground.sketchi.app/; agents use the MCP
endpoint and the HTTP API described below, both served from this origin.
Sketchi is MIT-licensed at https://github.com/shpitdev/sketchi.

There is no sign-in. Anonymous diagrams are addressed by artifact id and are
not tied to an account; treat them as temporary.

## MCP

Connect a Streamable HTTP MCP client to /mcp. The server is named
sketchi-code-mode and exposes three tools:

- docs: how to drive Sketchi, including the diagram spec shape.
- search: look up the Sketchi API surface before writing a call.
- execute: run Sketchi code mode, which builds flowcharts, mindmaps, sequence
  diagrams, timelines, charts, state machines, Gantt charts, ER diagrams and
  class diagrams, fetches artifacts, and applies diagram patches.

This is the recommended entry point for agents. Prefer it over the HTTP
endpoints below unless you need a single direct call.

## HTTP API

POST /api/v1/flowcharts/build
POST /api/v1/mindmaps/build
POST /api/v1/sequences/build
POST /api/v1/timelines/build
POST /api/v1/charts/build
POST /api/v1/state-machines/build
POST /api/v1/gantts/build
POST /api/v1/er-diagrams/build
POST /api/v1/class-diagrams/build
Build one diagram from a typed spec and store the result as an artifact.

POST /api/v1/generate
Generate a flowchart, mindmap, sequence, timeline, chart, state-machine, gantt, er, or class diagram from a prompt rather than a
prebuilt spec. Omit type for model selection, or pass a supported type as an
authoritative constraint. Unsupported native types return a typed error.

GET /api/v1/artifacts/{artifactId}?format=scene
GET /api/v1/artifacts/{artifactId}?format=excalidraw
Fetch a stored artifact. Add raw=true to receive only the file body, which is
what a download wants; omit it for the metadata envelope.

POST /api/v1/artifacts/{artifactId}/patch
Apply a patch to a stored diagram and record a new artifact.

These endpoints are same-origin: they do not send CORS headers, so call them
from a server or an agent runtime rather than from another site's browser page.

## Pages

/ — the playground itself.
/artifacts/{artifactId} — read-only review of a generated diagram.
/artifacts/{artifactId}/edit — the editable canvas for that diagram.
/examples/{exampleId} — read-only sample diagrams, for example
/examples/how-it-works and /examples/public-mindmap.
/projects, /projects/{projectId}, /diagrams/{diagramId} — saved Studio projects.
These are stored in the current browser only, not in an account.

## Elsewhere

https://sketchi.app/ — what Sketchi is, docs, and per-agent setup.
https://sketchi.app/llms.txt — the same overview for the main site.
https://icons.sketchi.app/llms.txt — the public SVG icon library and its API.

Native timelines: use `buildTimeline` (Code Mode) or `generate --type timeline` (CLI). Supply events with unique IDs, labels, and ISO dates at the source's precision (year, month, day, or instant with Z or offset) or explicit numeric order; optional `end` (phase), `kind: "milestone"`, `lane`, `today`, and concise descriptions are preserved. Dates and order cannot be mixed. The renderer spaces events by elapsed time, humanizes dates, and wraps long chronologies. No dependency scheduling.

Native charts: use `buildChart` (Code Mode) or `generate --type chart` (CLI). Supply `kind` (`bar`, `line`, or `pie`), `categories`, and `series: [{ name, values }]` with one value per category; optional `unit`, `categoryAxisTitle`, `valueAxisTitle`, `stacked` and `orientation` (bars), and `donut` (pies). The renderer draws nice-tick axes from zero for bars, value and percentage labels, a legend for several series, and leader lines for thin pie slices. Never supply coordinates.

Native state machines: use `buildStateMachine` (Code Mode) or `generate --type state-machine` (CLI). Supply `initial`, states with unique ids and optional labels (regular-state labels default to ids verbatim; `kind: "final"` for an end, `"choice"` for a guarded branch; states naming a `parent` form a composite with its own `initial`), and transitions with `source`, `target` and optional `event`, `guard` and `action`, drawn as `event [guard] / action`. Self-loops and transitions into or out of a composite are supported; composites do not nest.

Native Gantt charts: use `buildGantt` (Code Mode) or `generate --type gantt` (CLI). Supply tasks with unique ids, labels, a `start` day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and either `end` (last day, inclusive) or `duration` (calendar days); `milestone: true` draws a diamond. Optional `dependsOn` (finish-to-start predecessor ids), `phase` on every task (`phases` sets their order), `progress` (percent) and `today`. The renderer draws a to-scale date axis with day, week, month, quarter or year ticks, one row per task under phase headers, a date column, and dependency arrows routed clear of every bar and label. Never supply coordinates.

Native ER diagrams: use `buildErDiagram` (Code Mode) or `generate --type er` (CLI). Supply entities with unique ids (no dots) and fields written `"name type markers"` (`"id uuid PK"`, `"customer_id uuid FK"`, `"email text UK"`, `"note text?"` for nullable), and relationships whose `from` and `to` name `entity.field` or an entity, each end with a cardinality (`one`, `zero-or-one`, `many`, `one-or-many` or `zero-or-many`) and an optional label. The renderer draws each entity as a table and each relationship as an orthogonal line between the rows it joins, with crow's-foot ends; it owns every coordinate.

Native class diagrams: use `buildClassDiagram` (Code Mode) or `generate --type class` (CLI). Supply classes with unique ids (no colons or spaces), an optional `kind` (`abstract`, `interface` or `enum`) and members written as UML does (`"- radius: double"`, `"+ area(): double {abstract}"`), and relationships with a `kind`: `inheritance` or `realization` (`from` extends or implements `to`), `composition` or `aggregation` (`from` is the whole), `association` (`navigable: true` adds an arrow) or `dependency` (`from` uses `to`). Associations, compositions and aggregations take multiplicities and roles at each end. The renderer draws three-compartment boxes with superclasses above their subclasses and each relationship's UML head; it owns every coordinate.
